subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron/heartbeat authority be implemented as a narrow per-job/heartbeat marker now, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent trust boundary determines where authority is created, stored, audited, migrated, and revalidated for host exec.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader schedule-authority model so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one non-forgeable authority contract.

options.title: Implement Narrow Markers
options.body: Add explicit per-job and heartbeat elevated approval metadata now, with execution-time checks and docs, while leaving broader scheduling provenance for a later RFC.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevated authority by default and require explicit operator opt-in, accepting compatibility friction for existing cron and heartbeat setups.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader schedule-authority model so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one non-forgeable authority contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the adjacent cron caller identity implementation and proof path that this elevated authority model would build on.
